transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-01
Start: 15:30 PDT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jamal Reyes (AuroraCloud), Sara Lim (PM), Ben Ko (Eng)
Artifacts referenced: Deck: https://redwood.com/decks/auroracloud-integration-v1, Spec draft: https://redwood.com/specs/aurora-integ-draft, Aurora VPC doc: link to internal

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we got about 45 minutes on the calendar, gonna run through the marketplace integration flow, ref arch, and some open questions. jamal? want to open with your goals for the listing?
[00:28] Jamal: yeah thanks alex, um main thing from our side is make sure the listing meets AuroraCloud's marketplace gating — security, billing telemetry, and a clean install experience. we want customers to be able to subscribe and either use Redwood hosted or choose an Aurora-managed private deployment.
[00:50] Sara: and timeline wise marketing wants a draft listing by end of september, so we're looking at a pilot in the next 3-4 weeks if possible.
[01:12] Alex: ok good, that aligns. priya and i will outline the minimal required artifacts — integration spec, ref arch diagram, and a short install playbook.
[01:35] Priya: quick note, when we say "private" we mean a couple of modes: 1) Redwood Dedicated running in Aurora's marketplace infra (reserved capacity) and 2) Redwood Private - VPC peered or on-prem where Aurora spins up an instance of our runtime. each has different network/auth implications.
[02:00] Ben: can you clarify the peering model? aurora typically prefers VPC peering to avoid public internet egress; we also have strict CIDR ranges and require SAML SSO for admin console access.
[02:20] Priya: yep. for VPC peering we use a fixed set of egress IPs and we can provide an allowlist. K-V cache and batching traffic is internal to the cluster, shouldn't cross peering. also we support KMS integration for customer-managed keys — H-S-M or cloud KMS is fine but we need the key policy.
[02:48] Jamal: k-m-s? sorry the transcript picked up weird — S-A-M-L.. um KMS, yes we need the details since our compliance team will look. do you have a SOC 2 cert?
[03:10] Alex: yes, redwood is SOC 2 type II. we'll share the SOC 2 attestation and our security pack. also we have fine-grained RBAC in the console and SAML/SCIM support for provisioning.
[03:30] Sara: onboarding experience — what does the subscription flow look like? can customers start with hosted and then move to aurora-managed private?
[03:45] Alex: yep that's a common pattern. the marketplace listing shows the options: hosted API (no infra changes), dedicated/reserved, or private deployment. we leverage a deployment abstraction so users can pin model versions and rollouts regardless of underlying infra. migration requires KV cache warmup and some data sync steps.
[04:10] Ben: tell me more about the migration friction — how long is the cold start to move a customer off hosted?
[04:22] Priya: depends on model size and sequence lengths. for mid-size models, cold start with kv warmup is 5-15 minutes for initial latency stabilization; for very large models there can be longer warmups. we also recommend prefix caching and a short sync window.
[04:46] Jamal: on the listing we need to disclose latency SLOs, unit economics, and any constraints around quantized model variants. our customers will ask about cost differences.
[05:05] Alex: we'll put sample perf numbers in the listing based on our catalog; we'll also include Redwood Optimize recommendations — batching, quantization profiles, and expected token cost ranges.
[05:30] Ben: about quantization — does Redwood support INT8/FP16 profiles that play well with Aurora GPU types? our infra is primarily A100/RTX8000 equivalent.
[05:48] Priya: yes we support multiple quantization profiles. we pick kernels at runtime, but we should validate on your exact hardware. priya: (pause) i'll run a quick compatibility check on your instance types.
[06:10] Jamal: perfect. security-wise our procurement asks for KMS integration, audit logs and long-term retention for certain customers. can you export audit logs to our SIEM?
[06:30] Alex: yes we have export hooks, log forwarding (syslog/S3), and long-term retention options as an add-on. we'll include these in the spec doc.
[06:45] Sara: question: for marketplace billing, do customers get billed by Aurora or Redwood?
[06:55] Alex: marketplace listing can support either marketplace-billed (we integrate with Aurora's billing) or direct Redwood billing. that affects invoicing and revenue share. we'll capture options in the marketplace checklist.
[07:18] Ben: another technical: network egress and data residency. some customers need tokens to never leave region — is there a regional deployment we can reference?
[07:32] Priya: yes we can pin model serving to region and we have private deployments that run entirely within the customer's VPC. data residency options include local model hosting; we also support KMS that keeps keys in the customer's region.
[07:56] Jamal: ok good. next up: reference architecture diagram. alex, can you walk through the proposed arch?
[08:08] Alex: slide deck page 4 — canonical setup: Aurora marketplace provisioning calls Redwood Control Plane (we can host control plane or provide a customer-managed control plane), which orchestrates model serving on Redwood Dedicated pools or a private runtime in the customer's VPC. network flows: marketplace -> control plane -> serving nodes. for private mode, peering is between Aurora and customer's VPC or Aurora and Redwood private subnet.
[08:40] Sara: a quick callout — the control plane being hosted — does that transmit any customer data?
[08:50] Priya: control plane handles orchestration and metadata only; payload and inference tokens can be configured to go directly to the serving runtime depending on deployment mode. we can also enable end-to-end encryption with customer-managed keys.
[09:12] Ben: what about CI/CD for model updates, can Aurora trigger safe rollouts or do we need a webhook?
[09:23] Alex: we support rollouts via API webhooks and can do canary/A-B and automatic fallback policies. we'll include webhook examples in the spec.
[09:40] Jamal: regarding compatibility we'll need a short checklist for Aurora ops to validate before approving listing. something like network, KMS, SAML, RBAC, and billing mapping.
[09:58] Priya: yep we'll ship a checklist. also note about perf: batching and caching settings can change token cost; we recommend Redwood Optimize to compute expected costs based on traffic profile.
[10:20] Sara: is there a sandbox environment we can use to demo the flow?
[10:28] Alex: yes we can spin a short-lived sandbox deployment in Redwood Dedicated or provide demo keys for hosted API. for private env demos we'll coordinate with Ben to confirm capacity.
[10:45] Ben: for the sandbox please include sample traffic generator and a small prompt set so we can validate latency and cost.
[10:55] Priya: will do. i'll attach a prompt bundle and short perf harness.
[11:10] Jamal: procurement will need the SOC 2 and certs, also the data processing agreement.
[11:20] Alex: we'll attach our security pack, DPA, and pen test summary.
[11:28] Sara: one more thing — marketing wants a short joint solution blurb and logo usage guidelines. who owns that?
[11:36] Jamal: aurora marketing will own external listing copy but we need redwood assets.
[11:42] Alex: i'll send a 1-pager with value prop and logo assets.
[12:00] (small cross talk, background noise)
[12:30] Priya: technical question from bench — do you want to enable model-level quantization recommendations in the listing or keep it as an ops note?
[12:40] Ben: put it as an ops note. customers that care will dive deeper.
[12:50] Alex: ok ops note it is.
[13:10] (silence / typing)
[13:45] Alex: let's walk through the open questions we captured: 1) exact A100/instance types for compatibility, 2) peering IP/CIDR ranges, 3) KMS key policies, 4) billing flow preference. ben/jamal can you take those?
[14:05] Ben: i'll gather instance types and CIDR ranges; jamal will confirm billing preference.
[14:18] Jamal: yep i'll loop in finance and marketing and reply by next week.
[14:30] Sara: timeline recap — draft listing by end of sept, pilot early-mid sept, demo next week? there's slight overlap — maybe a demo week of 9/7 as alex mentioned.
[14:45] Alex: yes we'll aim for a hands-on demo week of 9/7; i'll send a Doodle after this.
[15:05] (timestamp jumps, mid-call deep dive)
[15:30] Priya: quick technical detail: our runtime uses continuous batching and KV cache; when you route requests via a peered private deployment, the KV cache lives on the serving cluster and never traverses public net. some transcribed notes earlier misread "K-V cash" but it's KV cache.
[15:55] Ben: good to confirm. any limits on batch sizes? we can tune but need the defaults.
[16:05] Priya: defaults depend on latency SLO; for sub-200ms p95 we'll recommend smaller batch sizes, for throughput use larger. we'll add recommended defaults to the config doc.
[16:30] Alex: another note for the listing: include a troubleshooting matrix — common failures (auth, peering, key policy) and quick fixes.
[16:44] Jamal: that will help our ops team.
[16:58] (background phone)
[17:20] Ben: regarding telemetry — do you export per-route token counts and cost breakdown? our finance team wants per-customer chargeback metrics.
[17:34] Alex: yes we provide token-level cost breakdowns, per-route and per-model dashboards in Redwood Console. we can send a sample CSV export format.
[17:50] Sara: please also add a sample SLA clause for marketplace listing — uptime, latency targets, and credits.
[18:05] Alex: we'll include a standard SLA template and note premium SLAs are an add-on.
[18:20] Priya: last technical note: for private deployments we support HSM-backed KMS integration but need the key policy and an admin principal. please share the ARN or HSM endpoint.
[18:40] Ben: will do.
[18:52] (brief pause)
[19:10] Alex: ok wrapping toward next steps — i'll send integration spec, a ref arch diagram, SOC2 and DPA, and a sample perf harness. priya will run compatibility tests on aurora instance types. ben will provide peering/CIDR and instance types. jamal will confirm marketing/billing preferences.
[19:40] Jamal: sounds good. one ask — can we get an internal runbook for common troubleshooting?
[19:50] Priya: yes we can draft a runbook and include escalation steps.
[20:05] Alex: any blockers that would prevent us from going to pilot in early september?
[20:12] Sara: main blocker is marketing calendar and procurement approvals; tech side seems manageable.
[20:22] Alex: fair. we'll do the checklist and demo next week to unblock marketing.
[20:35] (closing remarks)
[20:45] Alex: thanks everyone — i'll follow up with the spec and calendar invite. priya, ben, jamal, anything else?
[20:55] Ben: nothing more.
[21:00] Jamal: all good. thanks.
[21:05] (call ends, short notes)

Notes on transcript quality: Some words were auto-mis-transcribed (KMS / HSM / SAML), and speaker overlap occurred twice. See attachments referenced above.
